title: MATLAB Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Show a message
examples.description: disp displays a value. Single quotes can hold a row of characters.

examples.title: Name a value
examples.description: A variable stores a value. A semicolon hides the automatic display of an assignment.

examples.title: Make a row of values
examples.description: Square brackets build a row vector, which is a line of values.

examples.title: Read one position
examples.description: MATLAB indexing starts at 1. Parentheses select an item.

examples.title: Read a grid cell
examples.description: Semicolons divide matrix rows. A cell is selected by row, then column.

examples.title: Multiply each item
examples.description: The dot in .* means element-by-element multiplication. Each matching pair is multiplied.

examples.title: Make an evenly spaced row
examples.description: The colon form start:step:end builds evenly spaced values.

examples.title: Keep matching numbers
examples.description: A logical test makes a true-or-false mask for selecting values.

examples.title: Find an average
examples.description: mean returns the average. For this row it adds three numbers and divides by three.

examples.title: Use a condition
examples.description: if chooses a block of steps. end closes the block.

examples.title: Repeat counted steps
examples.description: A for loop visits each value in the row after the equals sign.

examples.title: Use an anonymous function
examples.description: An anonymous function is a short function value. @(n) names its input.
